archetype: single-storey roadside vehicle service garage with customer office, multi-bay workshop and rear service yard
ground_program: north-facing customer entrance from a main-road forecourt with a protected pedestrian path separate from vehicle bay approaches
customer reception and waiting room with direct sightline to the forecourt and service-bay doors
service counter connecting reception to a secure parts store and staff circulation
three vehicle service bays with full-width roll-up door openings and clear drive-through working envelopes
one two-post lift bay for underbody work and one inspection bay with a recessed service pit
mechanics workbench and tool-storage wall shared by the service bays without blocking vehicle circulation
parts store with shelving, tire rack and controlled access from both the counter and workshop
manager office with visibility into reception and workshop circulation
staff locker and washroom zone separated from the customer waiting area
compressor, electrical and fluids utility room isolated from public circulation
east-side secondary staff door to a fenced rear service yard with waste-oil storage, scrap bins and tire staging
graded paved forecourt tying the north bay doors and customer parking into the declared main-road connection
foundation course, drainage channel and utility stub connecting the workshop floor and service yard to surrounding grade
upper_program: partial parts-storage mezzanine above the rear support rooms, reached by an enclosed stair with landings at both ends
roof mechanical exhaust and make-up-air equipment positioned over the workshop and utility zones
no occupied upper floor above the vehicle bays so lift and vehicle clearances remain unobstructed
circulation: customer pedestrians move from the north forecourt to reception and waiting without crossing active service-bay work zones
vehicles enter each service bay independently from the north forecourt and can reverse to the forecourt without crossing customer parking
staff move from reception through the service counter to parts storage, office and the workshop through controlled doors
mechanics can circulate continuously behind the three service bays to tools, parts, utilities, lockers and the east service-yard exit
the enclosed mezzanine stair connects a real workshop-side landing to the parts mezzanine and does not terminate in open air
waste oil, tires and scrap move from workshop support spaces through the east staff door to the rear service yard without crossing the customer lobby
damage_constraints: preserve the north customer entrance, reception-to-workshop controlled route and at least two usable service-bay approaches
preserve the enclosed mezzanine stair and both of its landings wherever the mezzanine survives
concentrate primary roof failure over the eastern service bay and adjacent utility corner rather than deleting a rectangular volume
break the eastern bay facade with an irregular supported fracture and gravity-led rubble apron below failed wall and roof members
keep the western lift bay structurally legible with its lift or service equipment still identifiable
retain the rear service-yard route and enough fluids, tire and scrap handling evidence for the site's purpose to remain inferable
damage doors, windows and attached fixtures together with their supporting wall geometry so no floating openings or attachments remain
derive damaged and occupied variants only from this immutable clean master

required_manual_checks: the site reads immediately as a vehicle service garage from the main road rather than as a generic industrial shed
customer, vehicle and staff/service-yard circulation are visibly distinct and player-scale usable
all three service bays have credible vehicle working envelopes and operationally legible tools, parts and support spaces
the lift bay, inspection pit, parts store, utility room and rear fluids/tire handling form a coherent repair workflow
the mezzanine stair is enclosed, supported, has headroom and lands on real walkable floors at both ends
the paved forecourt, foundation, drainage and east service yard transition credibly into surrounding grade
damage preserves the garage program while following structural gravity and leaving no floating windows, doors, stairs, signs or roof fragments
